description: This line plot illustrates the results of an ablation study conducted on the HateXplain dataset, evaluating the impact of removing key components (Prompt, Augmentation, Attention) from a full model (“Ours”) on three performance metrics: Precision (purple line with circular markers), Recall (light blue line with circular markers), and F1-score (brown line with circular markers). The x-axis represents five experimental conditions — “Full model (Ours)”, “w/o Prompt”, “w/o Augmentation”, “w/o Attention”, and “w/o Prompt & Augmentation” — arranged categorically from left to right. The y-axis, labeled “Metric (%)”, ranges from 56% to 66% with major gridlines at 58%, 60%, 62%, 64%, and 66%. For the full model, Precision is 65.45%, Recall is 65.56%, and F1-score is 65.49%. Removing the prompt causes all metrics to drop sharply: Precision to 61.06%, Recall to 59.64%, and F1-score to 60.16%. Without augmentation, Precision recovers slightly to 62.22%, Recall rises to 62.63%, and F1-score to 62.22%. Removing attention leads to Precision at 64.06%, Recall at 59.17%, and F1-score at 59.67%. Finally, removing both prompt and augmentation results in Precision increasing to 65.44%, while Recall drops to 56.82% and F1-score to 57.74%. The plot visually demonstrates that while Precision is relatively robust to component removal, Recall and F1-score are more sensitive, especially when prompt or both prompt and augmentation are absent.
